present_facts: This is a hypothetical descent toward a town, not a canonical event. You are seventeen-year-old Angie. A mineral cart you hired has lost its ordinary wheel brake and is starting down a slope toward a footbridge. It carries your mineral purchase. Your wrist is painful from earlier work, and your footing is uncertain.

At the previous stop the carter showed you a reachable hand-brake lever: holding it may slow the cart long enough for someone to bring a wheel block, but you cannot know that it will hold. The carter has since left; only you and your junior are at this slope. Your junior is thirty paces away and can hear a shouted instruction. There is no suitable rune or spare jewel for stopping this cart magically, no other help already present and no injury to anyone yet.

You have a few seconds to choose what to say and attempt. The scene ends before the attempt succeeds or fails. Do not invent a completed rescue, new hazard, new power or the junior accepting an instruction before they answer.
You can see two townspeople on the footbridge in the cart's path. River noise prevents them hearing an ordinary warning at this distance. The cart has not yet reached them.
